## Introduction

A professional website requires more than informative content. Its visual appearance, organization, accessibility, and usability influence how effectively visitors engage with the information presented.

This portfolio demonstrates how Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) and Sassy CSS (SCSS) can extend Quarto's default website functionality to create a consistent professional identity.

## Understanding CSS and SCSS

### What is CSS?

Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) is a stylesheet language used to control the presentation of HTML documents. CSS allows developers to customize typography, colors, spacing, borders, positioning, and responsive layouts without changing the underlying content.

### What is SCSS?

SCSS is an extension of CSS that introduces additional programming features, including variables, nesting, reusable rules, and mixins.

Quarto compiles SCSS into standard CSS and integrates custom themes with the Bootstrap framework.

### Comparing CSS and SCSS

| Feature | CSS | SCSS |
|---|---|---|
| Browser interpretation | Direct | Compiled into CSS |
| Variables | Custom properties | Sass variables |
| Nesting | Supported in modern CSS | Supported |
| Mixins | Not native | Supported |
| Bootstrap customization | CSS overrides | Theme-level customization |
| Portfolio application | Component styling | Global design system |

## Customizing Quarto with SCSS

### Global Theme Variables

The `theme.scss` file establishes the global visual identity of the portfolio.

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/

$primary: #142b42;
$secondary: #245578;
$info: #86b6cf;

$body-bg: #ffffff;
$body-color: #334155;

$navbar-bg: #142b42;
$navbar-fg: #ffffff;

$headings-font-weight: 700;
$border-radius: 0.5rem;
```

These variables customize Bootstrap's default appearance and establish consistent styling throughout the website.

### Custom Styling Rules

The SCSS rules section defines additional styling for specific website elements.

```scss
/*-- scss:rules --*/

h1, h2, h3 {
  color: $primary;
  font-weight: 700;
}

.navbar {
  box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(20, 43, 66, 0.12);
}

.card {
  border-radius: 0.75rem;
  border: 1px solid #dce3eb;
}
```

Separating theme variables from styling rules makes the website easier to maintain and customize.

## Extending Website Components with CSS

The `styles.css` file provides additional control over individual website components.

### Reusable CSS Variables

CSS custom properties allow developers to reuse design values throughout a stylesheet.

```css
:root {
  --portfolio-navy: #142b42;
  --portfolio-blue: #245578;
  --portfolio-accent: #86b6cf;
  --portfolio-light: #f4f6f9;
  --portfolio-text: #334155;
}
```

Using reusable variables reduces repetitive code and improves design consistency.

### Custom Content Cards

The following CSS class creates a styled content container.

```css
.demo-card {
  background-color: var(--portfolio-light);
  border: 1px solid #dce3eb;
  border-left: 4px solid var(--portfolio-blue);
  border-radius: 8px;
  padding: 1.5rem;
  margin: 1.5rem 0;
}
```

## Integrating HTML with Quarto

Quarto supports Markdown alongside native HTML. This allows developers to create customized layouts and components beyond standard Markdown formatting.

For example, an HTML container can use a CSS class defined in an external stylesheet.

```html
<div class="demo-card">
  <h3>Customer Insights</h3>
  <p>Transforming customer data into actionable insights.</p>
</div>
```

Quarto also supports fenced divisions, which provide a Markdown-friendly alternative to HTML containers.

```markdown
::: {.demo-card}
### Customer Insights

Transforming customer data into actionable insights.
:::
```

Both approaches allow developers to apply reusable styling to website content.

## Responsive Website Design

Responsive design allows websites to adapt to different screen sizes, including desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices.

CSS media queries apply styling rules based on device or viewport characteristics.

```css
@media (max-width: 768px) {

  .profile-photo {
    max-width: 220px;
    display: block;
    margin: 0 auto 1.5rem auto;
  }

  .demo-card {
    padding: 1rem;
  }

  .btn-lg {
    font-size: 1rem;
  }
}
```

These rules help maintain readability and appropriate spacing on smaller screens.

Responsive design is particularly important for professional portfolio websites because recruiters and employers may access them from different devices.

## Accessibility and User Experience

Website customization should improve usability without creating unnecessary barriers for visitors.

The portfolio stylesheet incorporates visible keyboard focus indicators and reduced-motion preferences.

### Keyboard Navigation

```css
a:focus-visible,
button:focus-visible {
  outline: 3px solid #86b6cf;
  outline-offset: 3px;
}
```

Visible focus indicators help keyboard users identify interactive elements.

### Reduced Motion

```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {

  .project-card,
  .btn,
  .modebar {
    transition: none;
  }

  .project-card:hover {
    transform: none;
  }
}
```

This media query respects visitors who prefer reduced visual motion.

Additional accessibility considerations include:

- Appropriate color contrast
- Descriptive alternative text for images
- Logical heading structures
- Readable typography
- Meaningful navigation labels
- Accessible data visualizations

## Integrating Stylesheets with Quarto

### Website Configuration

The `_quarto.yml` configuration file connects the website to its custom SCSS theme and CSS stylesheet.

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: [cosmo, theme.scss]
    css: styles.css
```

### Dashboard Configuration

The dashboard uses its own format configuration to apply the same design system.

```yaml
format:
  dashboard:
    theme: [cosmo, theme.scss]
    css: styles.css
    scrolling: true
    embed-resources: false
```

Using both configurations helps maintain a consistent visual identity between standard website pages and interactive dashboards.
